title: Environmental Harm Menu Labels and Overall Dietary Quality
official: Longitudinal Trial Evaluating the Influence of Environmental Harm Menu Labels on Overall Dietary Quality
summary: The primary objective of this study is to evaluate whether repeated exposure to environmental harm menu labels on fast-food restaurant menus changes overall dietary quality. Participants will be randomized to view either a control (QR code) label or traffic-light style environmental harm labels on two alternating fast-food restaurant menus, and will order one lunch per week for seven weeks through a study ordering website, with each meal delivered to the participant the following day. The outcome is the change in overall dietary quality from baseline to endline, assessed with 24-hour dietary recalls before and after the seven-week ordering period.

interventions.name: Traffic-Light Style Environmental Harm Menu Labels

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Aged 18 to 64 years
* Consumes fast food two or more times per month
* Willing to eat meat
* Lives or works within the greater Washington, D.C./Baltimore metropolitan area, defined as the counties and county equivalents within the Baltimore-Columbia-Towson, MD and Washington-Arlington-Alexandria, DC-VA-MD-WV Core Based Statistical Areas (excluding Jefferson County, West Virginia)
* Has access to the internet during the daytime
* Has access to an internet-capable device (smartphone, tablet, or computer)
* Able to send and receive phone calls and text messages at a unique primary phone number (number if not affiliated with a separate prospective or enrolled participant record)
* Available to receive a weekly lunch delivery one day per week (Tuesday-Friday, 11:00 am - 3:00 pm) for seven weeks at a consistent address within the sample frame (this includes screening for potentially disruptive travel plans during ordering period)
* Within the delivery zone for both restaurants in the study
* Willing to complete training on lunch ordering procedures
* Willing and able to complete dietary recalls and surveys

Exclusion Criteria:

* Under 18 years of age
* Over 64 years of age
* Consumes fast food fewer than two times per month
* Pescatarian, vegetarian, or vegan (due to menu content)
* Lives and works outside of the greater Washington, D.C./Baltimore metropolitan area
* Lacks access to the internet during the daytime
* Lacks access to an internet-capable device
* Unable to send and receive phone calls and text messages at a unique primary phone number (phone number is affiliated with a separate prospective or enrolled participant record)
* Lives or works outside the delivery zone for either or both study restaurants
* Unavailable to receive seven weeks of consecutive lunch deliveries on a selected day Tuesday through Friday between 11:00 am and 3:00 pm at a consistent address within the sample frame
* Unwilling to complete training on lunch ordering procedures
* Unwilling or unable to complete dietary recalls and surveys
* Fails verification via Cloudfare Turnstile check when accessing REDCap Interest Survey
* Answers the hidden bot-detection question embedded in the Interest Survey
